scope.purpose: S1 class-inventory handoff for fresh-ship slice admission; evidence only, with no runtime or rollout change.
scope.contract_owner: Installed vertical-slicing skill, references/contract.md, Activation and migration; docs/configuration.md, Slice admission, identifies that owner.

finding.classification: Validation handoff coverage gap, not a substantiated runtime defect.
finding.invariant: Every affected call path and compatibility axis has an executable regression or an inspected unaffected reason, with evidence limits retained for the next phase.
finding.cause: The branch added admission and regressions without retaining the required class inventory.
finding.resolution: Map the shared admission boundary, sibling paths, input and output representations, lifecycle transitions and compatibility axes here using the existing tests/captures inventory convention.

regressions.interface: bin/fm-spawn.sh with real fixture Git repositories, temporary home policy and catalogue, and a fake terminal/Treehouse boundary; no live agent launch.
regressions.oracle: The accepted cut-3 intent and vertical-slicing Activation and migration contract require enforce refusal for configured fresh ships without a slice, observe delivery, and recovery/knowledge/supervisor/unconfigured bypasses; the recorded R1 decision preserves unlisted-project bypass even without a validator result.

cases.proves: A listed fresh ship is refused with the validator reason, receives its home/project/kind/task/brief arguments, and publishes no task record.
cases.rejects: Admission omitted or refusal ignored at the real spawn caller.

cases.proves: A declared slice launches and the executable validator receives the existing prep file as a second text input.
cases.rejects: Unconditional refusal or dropping the prep argument.
cases.limit: The stub accepts a declaration in either text; this is argument-wiring evidence, not proof of catalogue semantics or conflicting declarations.

cases.proves: Missing-slice findings produce a notice and successful launch in observe.
cases.rejects: Enforcing an observe policy or silently skipping its validator.

cases.proves: No policy and scout launches bypass the validator; a missing validator refuses a listed enforce ship and reports while launching in observe.
cases.rejects: Gating a scout/unconfigured home or silently admitting a listed enforce ship without its validator.

cases.proves: For both absent validators and validators exiting 2 without JSON, project other launches and publishes a record under enforce, observe and invalid modes while projects lists only proj.
cases.rejects: The original R1 unconditional dependency-failure refusal for unlisted projects.

cases.proves: A no-result validator reports in both modes; listed projects and null, string or non-string-member projects lists refuse enforce without a record and launch observe.
cases.rejects: Treating unreadable membership as an unconfigured bypass or weakening listed-project enforcement.

cases.proves: After a fresh admitted ship establishes a nonempty validator invocation log, a relaunch with a rewritten brief lacking SLICE leaves the cleared invocation log empty and emits no slice-admission message.
cases.rejects: The reported surviving mutant that invokes slice admission during relaunch.
cases.limit: The relaunch exit is deliberately unconstrained; this proves no gate consultation, not successful endpoint recovery. The brief is generated fixture input, not implementation-source inspection.

cases.proves: The actual installed Python validator refuses missing-slice and malformed-policy enforce spawns, reports and launches observe, and launches an unlisted enforce project with a task record.
cases.rejects: Stub-only agreement masking an incompatible installed validator or a broken real-validator R1 bypass.
cases.limit: The suite capability-skips an unreadable validator; only the explicit installed-validator pass in the retained output counts as real-validator evidence.

call_paths.inspection: The single fm_spawn_slice_admit call follows brief admission and precedes launch-brief rendering, backend allocation, worktree acquisition, branch setup, record publication and backlog commit. Both refusal and success return to this caller; no harness/backend-specific slice caller exists.
call_paths.gap: Refusal asserts no record; absence of branch/worktree/backlog mutation is established by inspected ordering, not separate side-effect assertions. Pre-existing admission locks and other admission checks are outside the slice guarantee.

call_paths.inspection: Missing/unreadable validators and unparseable/missing summaries converge on one fallback. It reads projects independently, bypasses only confirmed non-members, and otherwise applies observe versus non-observe behavior.
call_paths.gap: No-result fixtures use empty output/exit 2. Malformed JSON, malformed result objects and permission-denied validator files reach the same inspected boundary but are not separately exercised.

call_paths.inspection: Batch dispatch re-executes fm-spawn.sh once per pair. Deferred retry executes the saved spawn argv; neither caches a slice verdict. A subsequent fresh attempt therefore rereads the current policy through the same admission boundary.
call_paths.gap: Batch aggregation and deferred scheduling are inspected, not executed by this focused suite.

call_paths.inspection: The admission function returns before reading policy when RELAUNCH is 1. Control preflight sets RELAUNCH=1 and does not call slice admission; replacement spawn is passed --relaunch. Released-copy recovery uses the same relaunch flag.
call_paths.gap: Only direct retained relaunch is executed; control and released-copy routing are inspected. No claim of full relaunch success is made.

call_paths.inspection: Promotion updates an existing worker and sends its ship instructions; it does not enter the fresh-spawn caller added here. This cut changes fresh spawn admission only.
call_paths.gap: Promotion is not exercised and gains no admission guarantee from these tests.

representations.inspection: Policy is always FM_HOME/config/slicing.json. PROJ_ABS basename is passed both to the gate and the fallback membership check. The original brief carries the task body; prep is appended only when it is a file. FM_SLICE_VALIDATOR overrides the installed skills-master default. JSON summary and exit status determine reporting/refusal; no backlog or record schema is changed.
representations.gap: Default validator-path resolution is inspected; the focused installed case uses an explicit path. Full SLICE grammar, role rules, conflicts, revision skew and catalogue validation belong to the external validator and are not exhaustively tested here.

task_kinds_and_delivery.inspection: The shared boundary checks KIND=ship and RELAUNCH=0 only. Scouts and secondmates return before policy or validator access. Delivery mode and raw-command selection do not add a slice bypass for a fresh ship.
task_kinds_and_delivery.gap: Secondmate, no-mistakes, local-only and raw launches are inspected at the shared guard, not separately executed.

harnesses.inspection: The harness surface is bin/fm-harness.sh and spawn launch selection. fm_spawn_slice_admit reads no HARNESS, vendor output or process identity and receives no harness-specific arguments; every selected fresh-ship launch reaches the same call before agent delivery.
harnesses.gap: Portable fixtures select codex but launch no real vendor agent. No per-vendor version or real-harness compatibility claim is made.

backends.inspection: FM_BACKEND_KNOWN and FM_BACKEND_SPAWN in bin/fm-backend.sh list these ten. Shared slice admission precedes their backend-specific endpoint/worktree allocation, including Orca-owned allocation. The function has no backend branch. codex-app is outside the known/spawn sets and gains no path here.
backends.gap: Only the fake tmux terminal and fake Treehouse boundary execute; no live endpoint or non-tmux launch is proved.

platforms.inspection: Slice admission uses Bash, python3, basename and tail without a platform branch. Platform-dependent launch and terminal work remains downstream and unchanged. This cut adds no native Windows execution path.
platforms.gap: The retained output identifies the local execution platform. macOS and separate-host parity are unexecuted; no native Windows proof is claimed.

account_selection.inspection: Spawn resolves worker accounts before admission; slice admission reads no account, provider, model, credential or quota field. HOME affects only the default installed-validator path, while FM_HOME owns the policy and explicit FM_SLICE_VALIDATOR selects the tested installed validator. Every account that passes existing launch checks reaches the same admission call.
account_selection.gap: Fixtures isolate HOME and use ordinary selection. No login, credential, quota, alternate-account validator installation or provider call is exercised.

lifecycle_transitions.inspection: Fresh retries and follow-up task IDs remain RELAUNCH=0 and receive current policy admission; retained/released recovery preserves RELAUNCH=1. A refused slice check exits before task publication/backlog commit. No home policy is edited or switched to enforce by this branch.
lifecycle_transitions.gap: Backlog queue retention, concurrent policy changes, private rollout receipts and other homes are not executed here; enforcement activation remains a separate per-home decision.

live_validation_handoff.owner: Outer executor's designated validation phase; this review neither controls a pipeline nor runs other phases.

guards.scope: Existing real installed-harness identity/liveness guard; unchanged and not required to interpret the slice validator protocol.
Existing real Herdr lifecycle guard; unchanged and not proof of slice admission or a real vendor agent launch.

live_validation_handoff.status: Live guards were inspected, not run in this review. No new vendor-dependent classifier is introduced. Fresh live claims require the designated phase to retain date, versions, output and skips in docs/verification/runtime-backends.md.
live_validation_handoff.evidence_limits: The retained focused transcript proves only the cases that actually report pass. A capability skip is an open evidence gap, not installed-validator or live-runtime proof. No historical mutation run or red-before-fix execution is claimed by this evidence-only correction.
